author: Ramon Vredeling
title: More than any other product used to make lithium-ion batteri
text:
More than any other product used to make lithium-ion batteries there are real concerns about the limited supply of cobalt, which has pushed the price up in 2017. The problem: 60% of the world’s cobalt reserves are in the Democratic Republic of Congo ( DRC ). Interest in the battery metal has increased exponentially, and LME prices for cobalt have surged more than 120% in 2017. Cobalt is mined as byproduct of copper and nickel, linking its fortunes to those markets to some extent.

Companies with an eye on the lithium and cobalt markets include Apple ( AAPL ), Samsung ( OTC:SSNLF ), Toyota ( TM ), Tesla ( TSLA ), Ford ( F ), General Motors ( GM ), VW Group ( OTCPK:VLKAY ) and Buffet's Berkshire Hathaway co-owned BYD ( OTCPK:BYDDF ), China's number 1 EV company. Global carmakers have been lining up recently to announce plans to make their electric cars in the country, as under a new government scheme carmakers will earn credits for every electric or hybrid vehicle produced, and will be charged credits for every traditional fuel car they make.
Although the Tesla/Panasonic (PRCFY) Gigafactory in the Nevada desert may get a lot of headlines, it’s China that actually produces about two-thirds of the global supply of batteries for electric vehicles and about half of the 20 or more battery mega-factories currently in the works at located in the PRC. A recent attempt by one of the world’s biggest carmakers, VW Group, to secure long-term supplies needed for its push into electric vehicles was shunned by leading producers.
